reason: Attacked and it holds. I downloaded Gutenberg 33944, produced from Internet Archive images of the 1838 Charles Knight printing, and read the opening myself. The sentence is verbatim and is the first sentence of Martineau's own prose in PART I, REQUISITES FOR OBSERVATION, INTRODUCTION; above it stand only two epigraphs, the Latin tag Inest sua gratia parvis and a line from De Jouy, and below it comes A child does not catch a gold fish in water at the first trial. So the opening-sentence claim survives the obvious attack, which was that the epigraphs might make the claim false: they are quotations from other hands, not Martineau's text. The scanned title page reads LONDON: CHARLES KNIGHT AND CO. 22, LUDGATE STREET. 1838, with LONDON: PRINTED BY SAMUEL BENTLEY beneath it, so the imprint in the source line and in the evidence is right, and the table of contents puts INTRODUCTION at page 1, which supports the unclaimed page. No translation, so no drift. The line is Martineau's own, not a character's; nothing on the misattribution list touches it. shipped.js returns no shipped and no near line; Martineau is at one for the year from March, so this takes her to two of three, and she appears once in June. In scope: an 1838 treatise, not scripture, oratory, lyric or proverb. Publishable and, as an opening that admits how easily the eye misses what is in front of it, squarely on Truth and Clarity without being bleak. Tag Philosophy: the work is a methodological treatise, not a collection of essays, so Philosophy is the nearest true form in the closed vocabulary, and the lane's Essay floor is met by 06-phil-05 and 06-phil-06. Source line 120 characters, leads with the name, no dash; the quotation ends in a full stop and has no straight double quote.
